data.name: Annual usage cost
data.description: A lower annual usage cost means lower yearly expenses for running the refrigerator. While your costs may vary based on your electricity rates, a model with lower costs typically uses less electricity.
data.label: Annual usage cost

data.name: Counter-depth model
data.description: Counter-depth models usually measure 27 to 28 inches deep, not quite flush with the cabinets, but at least three inches shallower than many standard 36-inch-wide models. You can get models with stainless exteriors or panel kits.
data.label: Counter-depth model

data.name: Stainless/SS-look option
data.description: Stainless steel is stylish but it shows fingerprints. Another option: a vinyl-covered metal finish that gives you a stainless-steel look but resists smudging.
data.label: Stainless/SS-look option

data.name: Through-the-door ice/water dispenser
data.description: Through-the-door ice and water dispensers usually offer cubed or crushed ice and filtered water, but are only available on French-door models, with a special compartment in the fresh food section.  They add significantly to the purchase price--and according to our repair data, may also add reliability problems.
data.label: Through-the-door ice/water dispenser

data.name: WiFi
data.description: The refrigerator can connect to the WiFi in your home.
data.label: WiFi

data.name: Number of doors
data.description: Number of doors and/or drawers on front of unit.
data.label: Number of doors

data.name: Claimed capacity
data.description: Capacity of refrigerator is as claimed by the manufacturer.
data.label: Claimed capacity

data.name: Exterior height
data.description: Our measurement, including the top hinge and rounded up to the nearest inch. (We measured only tested models, but the similar models we list should have the same dimensions.) Built-in models have the compressor on top, making them about a foot taller than regular refrigerators. They fit flush with cabinets and counters.
data.label: Exterior height

data.name: Exterior width
data.description: Our measurement, including all protrusions and rounded up to the nearest inch. (We measured only tested models, but the similar models we list should have the same dimensions.)
data.label: Exterior width

data.name: Exterior depth
data.description: Our measurement, rounded up to the nearest inch. We include tubing or other protrusions in the back but exclude the handle. (We measured only tested models, but the similar models we list should have the same dimensions.)
data.label: Exterior depth

data.name: Total usable capacity
data.description: Usable capacity is the volume, in cubic feet, of usable interior space, based on our measurements. We included ice-makers in the storage measurements for top-freezer and bottom-freezer models, but not for side-by-sides.
data.label: Total usable capacity

data.name: CR's suggested refrigerator setting
data.description: This is the refrigerator section controller setting, typically in degrees but sometimes a numeric value, used for our 70 degree ambient temperature test to get the refrigerator center to be between 36 and 38 degrees.
data.label: CR's suggested refrigerator setting

data.name: CR's suggested freezer setting
data.description: This is the freezer section controller setting, typically in degrees but sometimes a numeric value, used during our 70 degree ambient temperature tests to achieve a center temperature between -1 and 1 degrees.  NA indicates that there is no separate freezer control.
data.label: CR's suggested freezer setting

data.name: Icemaker
data.description: Typically makes 3 to 4 pounds of ice a day--but according to our repair data, an icemaker may also add reliability problems. Some higher-end models have a feature to speed ice-making, which produces as much as twice the amount in the same time. Some Frech-door models have ice-making compartments in the fresh food section, if they also have through-the-door dispensers.
data.label: Icemaker

attrs.name: Thermostat performance
attrs.description: A high score means the refrigerator and freezer accurately reaches and maintains the temperature you set, even as room temperatures change. A top-scoring model helps keep your food stored safely at the right temperature with better consistency.

attrs.name: Temperature uniformity
attrs.description: A high score means the refrigerator and freezer keep temperatures consistent throughout, reducing warm and cold spots. A top-scoring model helps keep all your food at the temperature you set, no matter where it's stored.

attrs.name: Energy efficiency
attrs.description: A high score means the appliance uses less energy to cool more storage space. A top-scoring model can help you save on electricity bills without sacrificing food storage capacity.

attrs.name: Noise
attrs.description: A high score means the appliance runs quietly without making annoying noises.

attrs.name: Ease of use
attrs.description: A high score means the refrigerator has features like an external water dispenser, an ice maker, multiple interior lights, self-closing doors, and adjustable shelves. A top-scoring model typically has more features that make day-to-day use easier.

attrs.name: Crisper performance
attrs.description: A high score means the crisper drawer helps retain moisture, keeping stored produce from drying out. A top-scoring model's crisper drawers can help keep fruits and vegetables fresh for longer.

attrs.name: Icemaker performance
attrs.description: A high score means the ice maker produces more pounds of ice per day and typically offers greater ice storage capacity. A top-scoring model makes ice more quickly, likely has multiple ice makers, and ensures ice is available when you need it.

category_attributes.name: Door style
category_attributes.description: While most fridges have a flat, textured "skin," some have a smooth, curved surface that can't accept custom panels.

category_attributes.name: Pullout shelves/bins
category_attributes.description: These let you reach items in the back more easily. Some refrigerators have these features in both the freezer and main compartment.

category_attributes.name: Touchpad
category_attributes.description: In some models, you can use an electronic touchpad to adjust the temperature settings. In some higher-end models, the display will show the actual temperature.

category_attributes.name: Energy cost/yr.
category_attributes.description: Estimated cost in dollars, based on the current year's average national electricity rate. Your cost will vary depending on the rate for electricity in your area.

Built-in models have the compressor on top, making them about a foot taller than regular refrigerators. They fit flush with cabinets and counters.

category_attributes.name: Noise
category_attributes.description: A high score means the appliance runs quietly without making annoying noises.

category_attributes.name: Fridge usable capacity
category_attributes.description: Our measurement of usable volume.

category_attributes.name: Speed Ice
category_attributes.description: Temporarily boosts ice production for times when you need extra ice.

category_attributes.name: Child lock-out for dispenser
category_attributes.description: This feature, usually a button or switch, allows you to disable the ice and water dispensers. The icemaker continues to work while the dispensers are disabled.

category_attributes.name: Water dispenser
category_attributes.description: It is normally located on the front of the unit, or in the fresh food compartment if it has an internal dispenser.

category_attributes.name: Built-in water filter
category_attributes.description: A water filter, included with many icemakers, is intended to reduce levels of lead, chlorine, and other impurities. A filter usually adds to the cost of the refrigerator, so have your tap water tested to see if you really need one. Change about every six months; filter-cartridge-replacement costs range from $30 to $40, plus shipping.

category_attributes.description: The Overall Score blends our expert testing, predicted reliability, and owner satisfaction into one number—weighted to spotlight what matters most to help you choose quickly and confidently.

category_attributes.name: Half shelf
category_attributes.description: Half shelves, typically found on top-freezer or bottom-freezer models, can be set at the same height to provide a full-width shelf or can be set to different heights to improve storing flexibility.

category_attributes.name: Spillproof shelves
category_attributes.description: Shelf is designed to contain spills.

category_attributes.name: French-door style
category_attributes.description: French door models are bottom-freezer refrigerators whose upper compartments have two narrow doors that open similarly to the doors of a side-by-side refrigerator. These narrower doors use less space in front of the refrigerator when opened, and allow access to either or both sides of the full-width fresh-food compartment. Typically more expensive, French-door models are usually 36 inches wide, though some newer models are 33 inches wide.
